BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR MEDHI  ORDER 04.02.2026 Heard Shri D. Das, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Shri I. Das, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Shri P.K. Tiwari, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Shri K. Saxena,
learned counsel for the respondent nos. 1, 6 and 7 as well as Ms. P. Sangita, learned State Counsel,
A.P. for the respondent nos. 2 and 3.

The subject matter in this petition filed under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 read with Rule 9 of the Contempt of Courts (Gauhati High Page No.# 5/8 Court) Rules, 1977 is a judgment an order dated 10.02.2025 passed in two writ petitions.

entities.text: Contempt of Courts (Gauhati High Page No.# 5/8 Court) Rules, 1977
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: While WP(C)/230(AP)/2024 was instituted by the present petitioners
, WP(C)/242(AP)/2020 was instituted by the N.H.P.C. Ltd.
The subject matter of both the writ petitions was with regard to an Award dated 23.01.2019.

This Court after hearing the contesting parties had disposed of both the writ petitions, the relevant part of which is extracted hereinbelow:
"23.

Since Mr. Tiwari, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner/NHPC in WP(C)
No.242(AP)/2020 and respondent Nos.1, 4 and 5 in WP(C) No.230(AP)/2024 is agreeable to pay compensation to the respondent Nos.3 to 11 in WP(C)
No.242(AP)/2020 and petitioners in WP(C) No.230(AP)/2024 whatever they are entitled to under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, and since, Mr. Das, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners in WP(C) No.230(AP)/2024 and respondent No.3 to 11 in WP(C) No.242(AP)/2020 is agreeable to accept the compensation, whatever they are entitled to, under the said Act, this Court is inclined to dispose of both the writ petitions with following directions:-
Page No.# 1/8 vs Gaurav Kumar And 6 Ors on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19698249/
4 (a) The respondent No.2 in WP(C) No.242(AP)/2020 and respondent No.3 in WP(C)
No.230(AP)/2024 shall constitute a Board to reassess the compensation, which the petitioners in WP(C) No.230(AP)/2024 are entitled to, for acquiring this land at Bhismaknagar as per RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
(b) The Board shall be constituted with adequate representation of the NHPC.
Page No.# 6/8 (c) The Board shall assess the compensation, in each of the component, as specified in the First Schedule of RFCTLARR Act, 2013, in seriatum and further taking into account the provision of Section 29(2) of the Act of 2013, which provides for determination of value of the thing attached to the land or building.
(d) The respondent No.2 in WP(C) No.242 (AP)/2020 and respondent No.3 in WP(C) No.230 (AP)/2024, on his satisfaction about compliance of the all the provisions in assessing the compensation, by the Board so constituted shall pass the award Page 36 of 36 incorporating therein 12% interest per annum, on the market value of the land as provided under Section 30(3) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
(e) The aforesaid exercise has to be carried out within a period of 3(three) months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

(f) To facilitate re-constitution of Board and to make fresh assessment and to pass fresh award, the impugned award, dated 06.11.2018 approved by the Government of Arunachal Pradesh on 23.01.2019, stands set aside and quashed."

It is the case of the petitioners that though there was a direction for constitution of a Committee of the State and the N.H.P.C. Ltd., the same was not done and accordingly, the present petition for contempt was filed 14.05.2025.

The same was followed by filing of two interlocutory applications by the State, being I.A.(C)/132/2025 and I.A.(C)/149/2025 and the I.A. (C)/149/2025 was disposed of vide an order dated 10.06.2025 by granting further extension of two months for compliance of the direction.

Finally, vide a Page No.# 7/8 communication dated 16.07.2025 made by the Deputy Commissioner, Lower Dibang Valley, the appropriate land management department of the State was forwarded with the aforesaid Award which was approved on 28.07.2025.

The N.H.P.C. Ltd. has,
however, issued a communication on 29.07.2025 from which, it appears that the particular Officer was under the impression that further orders are required to be passed for disbursement of the amount in question.
The said Officer has been arrayed as the respondent no. 5 in the present proceedings.
Office note, however, reveals that there is no certainty regarding the service upon the said respondent no. 5.

Shri Tiwari, learned Senior Counsel, who appears for three of the Officers of the N.H.P.C. Ltd., has,
however submitted that the communication dated 29.07.2025 appears to have been issued with a wrong understanding of law which, however, is without any mala fide.

He has submitted that there Page No.# 1/8 vs Gaurav Kumar And 6 Ors on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19698249/
5 may be good grounds for challenging the present approved Award dated 28.07.2025for non-compliance of certain provisions of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This Court is, however, of the opinion that the final approval of the aforesaid Award was given by the Government way back in July, 2025 pursuant to a judgment which was passed on 10.02.2025 on extended period of time.
Almost eight months have elapsed since such approval.
In the backdrop of the aforesaid development, issuing the communication dated 29.07.2025 appears to be contemptuous on the face of it.

Be that as it may, Shri Tiwari, learned Senior Counsel has submitted that some time may be granted to have appropriate instructions with regard to the steps taken for compliance of the order in question.

Shri Das, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners has submitted that in Page No.# 8/8 the affidavit filed by the respondent nos. 1, 6 and 7, it has been pleaded that there is no element of contempt which appears to be supporting the justification of the communication dated 27.09.2025 issued by the respondent no. 5.
The said aspect would be taken into consideration at the appropriate time.
Be that as it may, as an exceptional circumstance, this Court grants time to Shri Tiwari, learned Senior Counsel to obtain necessary instructions.
Let this case be listed on 18.02.2026.
